aquariumdrunkard.title: CAN :: Karussell der Jugend, Soest 1970
aquariumdrunkard.description: No blueprint. Filmed by West German television in November 1970 at the Karussell der Jugend festival in Soest, this 84-minute document captures CAN with Damo Suzuki, Michael Karoli, Irmin Schmidt, Holger Czukay and Jaki Liebezeit, still exploring the possibilities of a sound that didn't quite resemble anything else. Repetition, interruption, groove and collective instinct. More than half a century later, the footage preserves the band before their influence had been mapped and their sound codified, when the music was still mutating in real time.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Wicker Man (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Part folk record, part pagan fever dream, The Wicker Man’s soundtrack is so steeped in sex, fertility, ritual and ancient melody that listening to it feels like stumbling upon something unearthed rather than recorded. Paul Giovanni’s songs create a world that feels simultaneously ancient and entirely invented—warm, earthy, erotic and communal, and perhaps all the more unsettling for sounding so beautiful.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Hawkwind: Do Not Panic (BBC Documentary)
aquariumdrunkard.description: A proper trip inside the Hawkwind mothership. This 2007 BBC documentary traces the band’s journey from the Ladbroke Grove underground through Space Ritual, Lemmy’s tenure, and their collision of rock, psychedelia, science fiction, and counterculture. Featuring interviews with Lemmy, Nik Turner, Michael Moorcock, Stacia and other Hawkwind alumni, it’s a window into a band where free festivals, naked dancers, cosmic poetry, motorways, and very loud amplifiers all somehow occupied the same universe.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Emily A. Sprague :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: In an album as lyrically economic as the startlingly beautiful Cyano , the latest solo release from Emily A. Sprague—familiar to many as the thoughtful anchor of indie-folk outfit Florist—even the few words we’re given can feel like lifelines. “We have to take care of ourselves” is one such arresting declaration. That reminder of self-preservation runs through Sprague’s ethereal ambient work, where emotion is conveyed less through narrative or explanation than through the feeling embedded in her evocative melodies.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Teenage Fanclub :: Do Not Dare To Dream
aquariumdrunkard.description: Few bands have aged like Teenage Fanclub. On their thirteenth record, the everlasting Scottish outfit embraces more of a soft focus on acoustics while maintaining their patented lilting and jangly elixir. Full of their unwavering and clear-eyed harmonies, the perceptive Do Not Dare To Dream continues TFC's path of challenging the tired notions of "reinvention" when the formula is this scientifically cathartic.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Peanut Butter Wolf
aquariumdrunkard.description: This week on Aquarium Drunkard Transmissions, Peanut Butter Wolf of Stones Throw Records. We hooked up for him to spin the yarn about how ST went from a small backpacker hip-hop imprint to an Adult Swim-boosted powerhouse, and how, 30 years in, the label’s roster is as diverse as ever, featuring post-punk, electro, future-forward R&B, and art-soul October 16, 17, and 18th in Highland Park at the ⁠Stones Throw 30 music festival. In this career spanning conversation, Wolf takes us back to the label’s earliest days, discusses his own major label experiences, and traces the thread that connects the Stones Throw artistic lineage.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Antonio Adolfo :: S/T 1972
aquariumdrunkard.description: Antonio Adolfo hated his 1972 solo debut. Intensely. He banned it from his official discography and denounced it whenever it resurfaced online. Yet the slightly off singing may be exactly what gives the self-titled LP its charm: there’s a Robert Wyatt or Scott Walker quality to Adolfo’s naturally dramatic timbre, with little bent edges creating tension against the jazz-inflected solos, basslines and gently cinematic arrangements. The result is a strange, beautiful record its creator wanted forgotten.

Of course the Artemis II astronauts who visited the moon earlier this year had state-of-the-art technology, not just housed in the vehicle, but in their pockets as well. nautilus.title: Scared of Shots? A Favorite Tune Helps Mute the Pain
nautilus.description: Many people really hate needles. When they have to give blood or get an IV for even a small medical procedure, they may panic, tensing up their muscles and spiking their heart rate, which can amplify the pain of the poke. Some people even suffer a sustained shock of pain and anxiety after the needle has come and gone. Trypanophobia , as this unfortunate condition is known, is not a rare phenomenon. A 2021 study in Psychological Medicine reported that it may afflict up to one in four adults in the United Kingdom. Trypanophobia can have terrible consequences for a person’s health: People who fear needles often skip vaccinations and other medical care. Read more: “How Music Sparks Imagination”
